description:
An AI-native vector design tool that turns prompts into editable product interfaces.

OpenPencil is an AI-native vector design tool with multi-agent workflows, a built-in MCP server, Figma import, and design-to-code export.

Why OpenPencil
🎨 Prompt → Canvas
Describe any UI in natural language. Watch it appear on the infinite canvas in real-time with streaming animation. Modify existing designs by selecting elements and chatting.
🤖 Concurrent Agent Teams
The orchestrator decomposes complex pages into spatial sub-tasks. Multiple AI agents work on different sections simultaneously — hero, features, footer — all streaming in parallel with per-member canvas indicators.
🧠 Multi-Model Intelligence
Automatically adapts to each model's capabilities. Claude gets full prompts with thinking; GPT-4o/Gemini disable thinking; smaller models (MiniMax, Qwen, Llama) get simplified prompts for reliable output.
🔌 MCP Server
One-click install into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Kiro, or Copilot CLIs. Design from your terminal — read, create, and modify .op files through any MCP-compatible agent.
🎨 Style Guides
Built-in style guide library with tag-based fuzzy matching. Apply visual styles (glassmorphism, brutalist, retro, etc.) to AI-generated designs. MCP tools for external agent access.
📦 Design-as-Code
.op files are JSON — human-readable, Git-friendly, diffable. Design variables generate CSS custom properties. Code export to React + Tailwind or HTML + CSS.
🖥️ Runs Everywhere
Web app + native desktop on macOS, Windows, and Linux — one Rust core, a single self-contained binary, no browser engine. .op file association — double-click to open.
⌨️ CLI — op
Control the design tool from your terminal. op design, op insert — batch design DSL, node manipulation. Pipe in from files or stdin. Works with desktop app or web server.
🎯 Multi-Platform Code Export
Export to React + Tailwind, HTML + CSS, Vue, Svelte, Flutter, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, React Native — all from one .op file. Design variables become CSS custom properties.
🧩 Embeddable SDK
op-web-sdk (vanilla) + op-web-sdk-react / op-web-sdk-vue adapters — embed a read-only .op viewer in your own app, powered by the same wasm renderer the editor ships.
🛡️ Design System Kit
Manage reusable UIKits with style switching and component composition. Import/export kits from .pen files. Built-in registry with MCP tools for external access.
👥 Real-Time Collaboration
Design together over authenticated peer-to-peer sessions with a public relay and built-in regional hubs. Join with a short pairing code, see live remote cursors, and resolve conflicts with per-edit detail and replay.
v0.8.5 brings the Rust editor to Android and iOS, alongside a redesigned
Studio Home and a more complete path from a brief to an editable design and
exported code. This release also improves multi-screen generation, reference
images, interactive previews, and the tools available to external agents.
Highlights
- Android and iOS editor shells. Touch editing, native file and account
  flows, and lifecycle-aware generation use the shared Rust engine.
- Studio Home and design workspaces. Start from a prompt or reference,
  compare design directions, and inspect generation results and quality reports.
- More faithful AI output. Planning and repair better preserve requested
  screens, supplied copy, image intent, and the geometry of repeated layouts.
- Interactive previews. Preview authored interactions, scrolling, and motion
  alongside the editable canvas.
- Websites and brands as starting points. Website import and brand
  extraction help turn existing visual material into editable design context.
- Code export for agents. Deterministic code export is available through
  MCP and the CLI; a lean MCP profile exposes a focused design workflow.
- Kimi Code integration. Desktop and daemon hosts can run text-only
  generation through the Kimi Code CLI, alongside existing provider integrations.
Android and iOS
The mobile shells share document rendering and editor logic with the desktop
app while using platform-native file pickers, sign-in screens, and lifecycle
handling. Touch selection, panning, pinch zoom, keyboard insets, and model-picker
gestures receive dedicated handling rather than relying on mouse input.
User-started generation can continue through supported background transitions:
Android uses a foreground service, and iOS uses the operating system's
background-processing allowance. Completion and cancellation are coordinated
with the engine lifecycle. These paths remain subject to system time limits,
power policy, and process termination; force-quitting does not preserve a
running generation task.
Android distribution uses a signed APK for direct installation and an AAB for a
later Play Console submission. Both are published with checksums in the GitHub
prerelease. The iOS release lane uploads to App Store Connect for TestFlight
processing. Neither lane automatically publishes an app to Google Play or
submits an App Store review.
AI Generation and Agent Workflows
- Multi-screen fallback planning keeps declared screens separate instead of
  silently folding them into one composition. Image prompts carry more precise
  subject, aspect, and label intent.
- Layout repair handles more repeated-row and calendar overflow cases, as well
  as text or glyphs hidden behind shapes. These checks supplement the model's
  output rather than treating a completed response as proof of a usable design.
- Chat attachments follow provider capability checks. Unsupported attachments
  produce an actionable error while preserving the draft and its images.
- Mobile chat work is bound to its document, page, tab, and account session, so
  late output from a replaced document or cancelled session is rejected.
- Codex sessions can continue reconnecting after a stream interruption, and
  Kimi Code gains a dedicated generation transport.
- MCP and CLI users can export code directly from the document. The lean MCP
  profile offers a smaller sequence for inspecting, generating, checking, and
  finalizing a design.
Editing and Reliability
The home screen's recent-file rows, mobile model picker, and touch cancellation
paths have been refined. Collaboration verification accepts valid signed
policy windows up to ninety days while retaining expiry and signature checks.
The release also updates runtime and TLS dependencies and tightens production
authentication archive verification.
Hosted Model Availability
The Hosted text-model runtime is shared by desktop, daemon, Android, and iOS,
including account-session checks and cancellation of stale requests. Publishing
v0.8.5 with Hosted enabled requires a reviewed, complete, signed ABI 4
authentication matrix and adoption of its release policy. Release and TestFlight
checks must verify that matrix and the ABI selected for each final link before
publication.
Hosted use also requires an active eligible plan, an available provider route,
and sufficient credits. An ABI 3 archive supports sign-in and collaboration but
cannot enable Hosted. Local Debug authentication overrides remain limited to
development builds. Hosted image input remains disabled under the current
billing capability contract.
Upgrade Notes
- Android and iOS artifacts follow their respective GitHub Release and
  TestFlight channels; TestFlight availability follows Apple's processing.
- Mobile builds use the same .op document model, but platform-specific export
  and background-execution limits still apply.
- CLI-based agent integrations run on native desktop or daemon hosts; the
  mobile engine does not launch desktop CLI processes.
- Source builds must use the adopted, signed authentication artifacts for
  production login and collaboration. Missing or mismatched release inputs
  fail validation rather than falling back to a local Debug archive.
